title: How Dynatrace and AWS create shared context for AI-powered operations
summary: Dynatrace earns the AWS Data Competency. See how Dynatrace and AWS connect data and production context to AI.
body_markdown:
We’re pleased to announce that Dynatrace has achieved the AWS Data Competency, recognizing our expertise in building unified, AI-ready data foundations on AWS.


Building and scaling on AWS means managing a vast, continuous stream of cloud telemetry and putting that data to work to drive better and faster outcomes. AI workloads need trustworthy runtime data, topology, and production evidence to validate outputs, investigate issues and act safely as organizations navigate the journey to autonomous operations.


This competency achievement adds a critical piece of the journey that extends from the core data and infrastructure powering AI to the intelligent workloads and autonomous operations running on top of it. In addition, our AWS AI Competency extends that validation into generative and agentic AI, while our competencies in Cloud Operations and DevOps reinforce expertise across the environments where those workloads are built and operated.


That breadth matters for production AI at scale. Effective management of Agentic systems requires proactively maintaining on the health and performance of their underlying. When something isn’t working as expected, Dynatrace gives your team a real-time view of the full-stack environment running AI agents and distributed data to understand whether the issue starts with the data, the application, the infrastructure, or the AI workload itself.


## How Dynatrace and AWS connect data and AI


Together, Dynatrace and AWS link the data foundation that AI relies on to the applications, AI workloads, and operational workflows that put it to work. Here’s what that means for you.


**What you need to do** **How Dynatrace and AWS help**


Bring your data together Understand the AWS data and infrastructure your applications and AI workloads depend on via the Dynatrace Clouds App


Build with context Bring production context into development workflows with Kiro and Bluebox by Dynatrace


Operate AI with confidence See how AI workloads behave alongside the applications, infrastructure, and dependencies around them


Investigate issues faster Give AWS DevOps Agent Dynatrace production context so teams spend less time assembling evidence


Move toward autonomous operations Give agents the evidence to investigate and propose actions while keeping people in control


## Start with data that has context


**The journey starts with data.** AWS environments generate logs, metrics, traces, events, and other signals across cloud services. But collecting telemetry is only part of the job. You also need to understand how those signals relate to one another: which services depend on each other, what changed, and what else was affected.


Dynatrace natively ingests your AWS environment via the Clouds App and brings that observability data into Grail™, where teams can analyze runtime telemetry alongside topology to understand how services and dependencies are behaving as the environment changes. Rather than piecing together an issue across separate data sources, teams can see what is happening across the AWS environment and how its components relate to one another.


That runtime view matters as AI becomes part of the environment. AI workloads and agents rely on the data and infrastructure beneath them, and issues at that foundation can affect what happens further up the stack. The AWS Data Competency provides third-party validation of Dynatrace expertise at that foundation.


## Build and operate AI with context


As AI moves into production, observability needs to extend to the AI workloads themselves. Dynatrace’s observability powered by AI helps teams understand AI workloads in the context of the applications, infrastructure, and dependencies around them. Integrations with services such as Amazon Bedrock AgentCore extend that visibility into agentic workflows running on AWS.


That context can follow AI across its lifecycle on AWS. Developers can use production evidence as they build and troubleshoot applications. As those applications move into production, teams can understand how the AI workload is behaving alongside the environment it depends on. The same context can then inform AI-assisted operations.


This work is backed by AWS validation. In September 2025, Dynatrace achieved the AWS[Generative AI Competency](https://ir.dynatrace.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/393/dynatrace-achieves-the-aws-generative-ai-competency) , recognizing our technical proficiency and proven customer success in helping organizations monitor and govern generative AI application in production.*


> *The AWS Generative AI Competency is now called the AWS AI Competency


## Put production context to work


Understanding what happened is only useful if teams can act on it. Dynatrace Intelligence brings production evidence into the tools and interfaces where teams already work, so they can use what’s happening in the environment without having to piece it together somewhere else.


That becomes even more important as AI agents take on investigation and action. They need the same runtime evidence teams rely on to understand what changed, which services are connected, and what else is happening around an issue.


### Build with context using Kiro and Bluebox


Production context can be useful before a change ever reaches users.


Kiro and Bluebox by Dynatrace bring that context closer to development, connecting what developers intend their software to do with evidence of what it’s actually doing in production.


The Kiro Agent integration, for example, uses Dynatrace vulnerability signals to propose targeted code fixes, open pull requests, and verify remediation. It uses governed, real-time context through the Dynatrace Model Context Protocol server. Developers know what software is intended to do. Production context provides evidence of what it’s actually doing.


Bringing the two together gives your developers better information as they investigate issues and evaluate changes.


### Investigate incidents with AWS DevOps Agent


The Dynatrace integration with AWS DevOps Agent brings Dynatrace production context into AI-assisted incident investigations. Instead of asking your teams to piece together an incident across separate tools, observability context can become part of the investigation itself.


Joint users have seen up to a 70% reduction in MTTR, which shows that observability data doesn’t have to stop at an alert or dashboard. It can become evidence for AI-assisted operations, helping teams understand what happened and decide what to do next.


### Help SRE teams move toward autonomous operations


The same principle extends to site reliability engineering through the Dynatrace SRE Agent.


The SRE Agent can investigate a problem, build a root-cause analysis from relevant evidence, and add that analysis directly to the Dynatrace problem. That means the next responder can start from an existing analysis rather than a blank investigation.


Human oversight still matters though. The SRE Agent is autonomous where teams want it and human-approved where needed. That combination of production context, AI-assisted investigation, and human oversight is important as teams move toward more autonomous operations.


AI doesn’t make production context less important. It makes good production context more valuable.


## A partnership that keeps evolving


The AWS Data Competency adds another dimension to the Dynatrace and AWS relationship. It builds on the value we’re creating together to help your teams connect data and production context to AI-powered operations.


[See this partnership in action at AWS re:Invent](https://www.dynatrace.com/aws-reinvent/) , where we’ll show how Dynatrace and AWS bring production context into development and operations powered by AI.
